title: World Brief · Monday, November 9, 2026
subtitle: Prepared 19:05 ET

items.title: Trump: Iran war is militarily "effectively over"
items.text: After meeting Qatar's prime minister, Trump said a new strike is very unlikely while talks continue; Brent fell 5.5% to below $93. But attacks on ships around Hormuz continue and the Houthis claimed an attack on Aramco offices in Riyadh, so the drop in oil is fragile.

items.title: Nvidia board opens probe into Jensen Huang
items.text: The board launched an independent review over allegations about Huang's relationship with a businessperson suspected of gathering information for China; Trump said the FBI is looking into it but that Huang "will be fine". The stock fell 4.6% (~$200 billion in value). The company said it sees no sign of leaked secrets and China rejected the claims; the allegations are not proven.

items.title: Washington wakes up to a new balance
items.text: Congress convened this week after Democrats won both chambers in the midterms; Trump made Stephen Miller White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles. Republican Thomas Massie filed impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Hegseth over the Iran war, and a House vote may be forced.

items.title: Fed: a December hike is being priced in
items.text: The Fed raised rates 25 basis points in September and held at 3.75-4.00% in October; futures put the odds of another hike in December at ~80%. Tuesday's October CPI at 08:30 ET is critical; because of the 2025 shutdown, no annual rate will be published this time.

items.title: Race to succeed Lagarde at the ECB
items.text: Euro area finance ministers (Eurogroup) reviewed candidates for when Lagarde leaves on February 7, 2027; Klaas Knot and BIS chief Pablo Hernandez de Cos are the front-runners. The choice matters for the euro and Europe's rate path; the euro approached 1.12.
